1947, October 4.
The following is a faithful transcription of the carbon copy of the typed original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, C.F.K. Cap.
SALUT FELIX CAFUCHIT FRIARY. SU RINGTON, INDIANA October 4th 1947. FEAST OF SAINT FRANCIS.
Dr. J. P. Young. 616 Forth Jefferson Ave. City.
My Dear Doctor Young:
Kay the Lord give you his peace!, you and yours - that peace of which the "world" knows little or nothing; the peace which St. Francis was so astonishingly successful in promoting, the peace to establish which, the Second Person of the Blessed Trinity came down from Heaven and lived, suffered and died as man and the promoters of which, "shall be called the children of God".
I have been wanting to write you Doctor but I feared to embarrass you. I have wanted to talk things over but you've escaped me. I was pleased at your bringing that, "Companion of the Summa", as you called it. I would wish to have seen more of it and to have talked it over with you - in connection with the primary purpose of my visit. For, to be frank, much as I appreciate your treatments and miss them and thank you for them, they must be altogether of secondary importance in face of the condition of your immortal soul and the danger of which I see you to be in of losing it together with your faith in God and His Church.
I was happy to see you, as it seemed to me, that you were trying to do the right thing and to be happy. To the rational creature it must mean the same thing. I still hope you are trying. What more can any of us do? Its all the Good God requires or expects of us. - TO TRY. Success must depend on Him. He does expect, however, and He will be the Judge as to whether we will have used the means He offers to insure the success He expects and which His justice will demand.
Alas for humanity! How sadly few comparatively, ever think of such an obligation? - Alas! Hence the want of peace for the individual. hence the turmoil! - domestic; - national, - international! Everyone seeking peace, - as positively as the stone in the air seeks rest - and there is no peace for the rational creature except in the willing service of its Creator.
